bull_bear.body:
- Leverage has fallen sharply: the Debt to Equity (x) chart shows 2.4, 2.5, 2.1 and 0.8 against FY23, FY24, FY25 and FY26.
- FY26 saw a large equity infusion — equity share capital rose from 82.0 to 103.6 Rs Cr and other equity from 297.1 to 820.6 Rs Cr (FY25 to FY26), with Cash Flow from Financing Activities of +402.5 Rs Cr in FY26 against -93.3 Rs Cr in FY25.
- The business is working-capital hungry: FY26 shows Changes in Working Capital of -378.5 Rs Cr and Net Cash from Operating Activities of -166.3 Rs Cr, against FY26 inventories of 1,039.5 Rs Cr, trade receivables of 495.2 Rs Cr and current borrowings of 757.4 Rs Cr.
- Fixed-asset intensity is low and falling: FY26 property, plant and equipment of 87.9 Rs Cr (from 101.8 Rs Cr in FY23), capital work-in-progress of 1.7 Rs Cr, and Cash Flow from Investing Activities of just +0.5 Rs Cr in FY26.
- The deck states no dividend policy, buyback or capital-allocation framework.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- Claims a place among "India's top three basmati rice producers and exporters", with 4+ decades in operation and the AEROPLANE brand described as "a trusted anchor brand with strong recall, ensuring customer loyalty and margin stability despite rising costs".
- Integration is the stated moat: "One of few players with end-to-end basmati value chain", spanning procurement, processing, packaging and sales with dedicated quality-assurance teams.
- Credentials cited: Three Star Export House status, ISO 22000:2018 & HACCP accreditation, and 100 registered trademarks (70 in India, 30 across 26 countries primarily in Europe, Asia and Africa) plus 22 copyrights in India.
- Global reach of 38 countries via 53 overseas distributors with "strong Middle East demand" and repeat orders, alongside 436 domestic distributors across GT, MT, e-commerce and D2C.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Industry] Citing a CARE Report, the deck states India was the largest rice exporter in MY 2024-25 accounting for 40% of world exports, that Asian countries accounted for 74% of global share in MY 2024-25, and that India exported basmati to 150 countries with the Middle East (Saudi Arabia, Iran, Iraq, UAE, Yemen) as the major destination.
- [Industry pricing] The All-India average rice price trend chart runs from 31.7 to 44.1 Rs./Kg across the 2019 to 2024 period shown (source: CARE Report).
- [Risk flagged by the deck] "Rice cultivation is highly susceptible to changes in weather patterns and government interventions impacting prices and thus affecting yields."
- [Corporate structure] The growth-story timeline lists incorporation as a public limited company in 2003, acquisition of the promoter's proprietorship M/s. Amir Chand Jagdish Kumar (including all assets, liabilities and units), incorporation of ACJK Foods Private Limited as a wholly owned subsidiary, an IPO and listing on the exchanges, and set-up of a subsidiary in Singapore — the year label for each milestone other than 2003 is not reliably recoverable from the extract.
- [Promoters and board] Promoters Jagdish Suri (Chairman & Managing Director, 4+ decades in the rice industry, leading procurement, domestic sales, operations and finance) and Rahul Suri (Whole Time Director, 30+ years, heading production, exports, quality control and marketing); Ramnika Suri is a Non-Independent Director (22+ years); independent directors include Gauri Shankar (39+ years in BFSI, former MD & CEO at PNB International, PNB Gilts and PNB Housing Finance).
business.title: Notable from the deck

deepdive.thesis: The deck positions Amir Chand Jagdish Kumar (Exports) Limited as "one of India's top three basmati rice producers and exporters, powered by its flagship AEROPLANE brand", running a fully integrated ~550,800 MTPA farm-to-consumer platform at ~61% utilisation while diversifying into branded FMCG kitchen staples.
